inputs.sbc_source: FY2026E = 9M FY2026 actuals (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, cash-flow statement: equity-based compensation $95m, employee equity-award withholding taxes $62m in financing) plus Q4 at the 9M run-rate (~$30m SBC, ~$2m withholding). JCI publishes no combined SBC-plus-withholding figure, so the two cash-flow lines are summed. FY2025 actual for reference: SBC $140m + withholding $49m = $189m.
inputs.share_count_basis: 605.74m ordinary shares outstanding at 2026-06-30 (Q3 FY2026 10-Q cover) plus 2.0m dilutive awards (Q3 FY2026 EPS denominator table: basic 608m, diluted 610m weighted). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. JCI is an active repurchaser (FY2025 $5,991m including the ~$5bn ASR funded by the Bosch proceeds; 9M FY2026 $850m), so the flat count is funded, not a modelling convention.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.2 x ERP ~4.75% = cost of equity ~9.9%; after-tax cost of debt ~3.9% (avg coupon ~4.8%, 18% cash tax); D/V ~9.5% at the current market cap. Computed ~9.3%; rounded to 9.0%, the same in every scenario (risk lives in the scenario flows and weights, not the discount rate).
inputs.lease_treatment: ASC 842 operating leases: lease cost is an operating expense already inside the EBITDA margin (treatment B), so the ~$1.3bn of operating lease liabilities (FY2025 10-K: $226m current + $1,084m non-current) are EXCLUDED from net debt. total_debt is short-term debt + current LTD + LTD only, per the 10-Q capitalization table.
inputs.nci_treatment: Consolidated flows; noncontrolling interests at book ($33m, 2026-06-30) deducted once in the equity bridge. NCI is immaterial post the Hitachi JV sale (continuing-ops NCI income $7m in 9M FY2026).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial'; adaptations file read for leases, NCI, WC sign and charge-risk-once). Fresh build; no prior DCF and no MEMORY entry. FY0 IS AN ESTIMATE: the fiscal year ends 2026-09-30 (tomorrow) and is unreported, so FY0 = FY2026E built from 9M FY2026 actuals plus Q4 at guidance: revenue = 9M $18,553m + Q4 ~$7,035m (Q4 FY2025 $6,442m x guided organic +9-10%, less ~$45m divestitures, plus modest FX) = ~$25,590m; adjusted FCF = ~100% of guided adjusted NI (~$5.05 x ~611m diluted = ~$3,090m; 9M adjusted FCF was $2,133m). FY2025 actuals for the record (continuing operations): revenue $23,596m; OCF $2,554m; capex $434m; reported FCF $2,120m; owner FCF $1,931m. Using the June-2026 balance sheet with FY2026E flows leaves Q4 FY2026 FCF (~$0.9-1.0bn) outside the model, the normal one-quarter lag and conservative. The R&LC HVAC business (sold to Bosch 2025-07-31) is discontinued operations throughout: all figures are continuing-ops and every historical row FY2022 onward is recast on that basis; FY2020-21 in the CSV still include R&LC, so the 5-year revenue CAGR mixes bases and is not used. EBITDA MARGIN BASIS: pre-SBC (the engine deducts SBC separately) and AFTER a ~1.4pp haircut to the company's adjusted EBITDA for the recurring share of 'non-recurring' restructuring, transformation and transaction costs (FY2023 $1,049m, FY2024 $510m, FY2025 $546m of restructuring alone; LTM June-2026 restructuring $624m + transformation $253m + transaction $55m, of which roughly $370m/yr is cash). Company adjusted EBITDA LTM June-2026 $4,553m (18.2% of LTM revenue, 18.7% pre-SBC); FY2026E owner basis ~17.1%. AFFF settlement payments and insurance recoveries, mark-to-market and divestiture gains are excluded from the base. Interest income is not stripped: JCI carries $8.8bn net debt and interest income is immaterial inside net financing charges. Cash tax: adjusted ETR guided ~17% (Irish plc, Pillar Two floor 15%); cash taxes paid have run above book (FY2024 $704m, FY2025 $606m on ~$1.5-2.0bn pretax, though those years carried discontinued-ops and discrete taxes), so the base ramps 18% -> 20%. Working capital: AR $6,970m + inventories $1,955m exceed AP $3,917m + deferred revenue $2,943m, so growth consumes cash; wc_capture -5% of the revenue change (deferred revenue and customer deposits on data-center orders partly offset). Qualitative context from JCI_Analysis.json (2026-09-29).

equity_bridge.note: Q3 FY2026 10-Q balance sheet, 2026-06-30; charged once here, flows are consolidated

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: Base-case FY2027-31 average revenue growth (guided FY2026 organic ~8%, Q4 exit rate 9-10%, backlog $21.0bn +32% organic, orders +27%), decelerating to 3% by FY2035. Equity CAGR is rejected as the anchor: it is negative (-6.9%/yr) purely because $6bn of FY2025 buybacks shrank the equity base, and the 5-year revenue CAGR (1.1%) mixes pre- and post-R&LC-divestiture bases.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.9% 5yr, -9.4% 3yr) diverges from revenue (+4.6% 3yr continuing) and EPS by far more than 30%: the equity base was cut by the FY2025 $5,991m repurchase (Bosch proceeds) and the R&LC carve-out, not by losses. EPS CAGRs are on continuing-ops GAAP EPS ($2.20 FY2022 -> $2.63 FY2025; FY2020 $0.84 was a trough year), not the reported FY2025 total EPS of $5.04 which carries the $1.57bn Bosch gain. Owner-FCF CAGRs: 3yr from a FY2022 trough ($601m, factoring unwind and working-capital build) is not meaningful; 5yr owner FCF is flat ($1,928m FY2020 -> $1,931m FY2025) while FY2026E steps up to ~$2.9bn on the margin inflection.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series (continuing OCF - capex - SBC - equity-award withholding taxes; interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 $1,928m; FY2021 $1,890m; FY2022 $601m; FY2023 $1,266m; FY2024 $943m (FY2024 continuing OCF $1,568m depressed by the AFFF settlement and factoring wind-down); FY2025 $1,931m; FY2026E ~$2,901m. SBC + withholding has been flat at ~$110-190m/yr, so the owner-FCF and reported-FCF CAGRs agree: SBC is not absorbing the growth.

base.growth_rationale: FY2027 +8% on a $21bn backlog (+32% organic) and 9-10% Q4 FY2026 exit rate; data-center thermal demand carries FY2027-28, then growth fades to GDP-plus as the AI-capex wave normalises and EMEA/China stay low-single-digit.
base.margin_rationale: Pre-SBC, post-haircut owner EBITDA margin from ~17.1% FY2026E to 19.5% by FY2034: ~45-50% operating leverage on FY2027-29 growth plus the Weidemanis productivity program, ending ~1pp below Trane-class levels. Company-basis equivalent ~21% adjusted EBITDA.
base.da_rationale: D&A 2.6% of revenue FY2026E, falling as acquired-intangible amortisation runs off; only the tax-deductible share is carried (depreciation ~1.3% plus part of amortisation), so the tax shield is not overstated.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 1.8%, 9M FY2026 1.3%; 1.5-1.6% allows capacity additions for data-center chillers and CDUs.
base.tax_rationale: Adjusted ETR guided ~17%; cash rate ramps 18% -> 20% for Pillar Two and the historical cash-over-book gap.

bull.narrative: Backlog converts at double-digit growth for three years, margins reach Trane-class 21.5% (owner basis), tax holds near the guided 17-19%.

bear.narrative: Data-center capex digestion from FY2028 with a FY2029 revenue decline; margin program stalls; restructuring stays a permanent cost; cash tax drifts to 21%.

scenario_narratives.base: JCI's axes are (1) how long the AI data-center cooling wave sustains double-digit Americas orders, (2) whether the new CEO's Danaher-style operating system converts 45-50% operating leverage into a durable 2-3pp margin step-up, and (3) how much of the perennial restructuring/transformation spend is truly non-recurring. Base: the $21bn backlog delivers +8% in FY2027 and +7% in FY2028, then growth fades to 3% by FY2035 as hyperscaler capex normalises and EMEA/APAC stay low-single-digit; owner EBITDA margin (pre-SBC, after a ~1.4pp haircut for recurring 'one-off' charges) rises from ~17.1% to 19.5%; capex 1.5-1.6%; working capital consumes 5% of incremental revenue; cash tax 18% -> 20%. Terminal 2.5% growth at 9% WACC (Gordon ~15.8x binds below the 17x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: Hyperscaler and AI-factory demand persists through the decade and JCI's chiller/CDU share holds against Trane and Carrier: revenue compounds +11%/+10%/+9% for FY2027-29 and is still growing 5% in FY2033; the business system takes owner EBITDA margin to 21.5% (company basis ~23%), the restructuring haircut effectively disappears into productivity; cash tax stays near the guided 17-19% Irish-plc rate; terminal 3.0% with a 19x cap (Gordon ~17.2x binds).
scenario_narratives.bear: The data-center thesis is a capex cycle: orders roll over in FY2028 and revenue falls 3% in FY2029 as hyperscalers digest, with China and the Middle East still soft; margins slip back toward 15.6% as operating leverage reverses before recovering only to 17%; restructuring and transformation stay permanent; asbestos/AFFF and tariff costs bite; cash tax settles at 21%. Terminal 2.0% with a 15x cap.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 20% because JCI's growth story is now concentrated on one identifiable cycle, AI data-center capex, and its equipment half remains tied to non-residential construction; a digestion phase is a real, dated downside axis, not a generic risk. Bull cut to 30% because the bull case needs two things to hold together over a decade: sustained hyperscaler spend AND full delivery of a multi-year margin program by a new management team, while Trane and Carrier are attacking the same niche. The balance sheet (1.9x net debt/adjusted EBITDA) carries no solvency element, so the bear is a cyclical earnings path, not a going-concern case.

valuation_philosophy.summary: JCI is valued as a cyclical industrial compounder on owner FCF: continuing-ops cash flow after SBC and equity-award taxes, with the company's 'adjusted' EBITDA haircut for the recurring share of restructuring and transformation costs, discounted at a single 9% USD WACC, with leases as operating cost, NCI charged once in the bridge, and a terminal value that never exceeds the 17x cap. The current price gives full credit for the data-center backlog and the margin program; the model's job is to say what those are worth to a buyer demanding a 15% return and to show, via the required-return table, what return the market price actually implies on the base path.
key_risks_to_valuation: FY0 is an estimate (FY2026 ends 2026-09-30, unreported): if the Q4 print misses the guided ~9-10% organic growth or ~$1.55 adjusted EPS, the base revenue and margin anchors move with it.
AI data-center capex digestion: orders (+27%) and backlog (+32%) are the growth evidence; a hyperscaler pause removes the FY2027-28 growth years the base case relies on.
The ~1.4pp restructuring/transformation haircut is a judgment: if these costs genuinely end, the base is ~$0.35bn/yr too low; if they persist at the LTM $0.9bn P&L level, it is too high.
Cash tax: an Irish plc guiding ~17%; the model's 18-20% ramp costs ~$3-4/share versus the guided rate, while a US or OECD challenge to the structure would cost more.

Legacy asbestos and AFFF liabilities are outside the bridge (asbestos largely funded by restricted investments; the $750m AFFF settlement mostly paid with insurance recoveries offsetting); a further adverse ruling would be a direct deduction.
Terminal value is 55-60% of enterprise value; a 1pp change in WACC moves the base value by roughly 15%.
